claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy contains coarse dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Coarse interlamellar spacing and internal colony boundaries facilitate microcrack nucleation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
High-pressure torsion can be applied as a post-solidification severe-plastic-deformation treatment to a high-entropy alloy.
High-pressure torsion will refine the dual-phase lamellar spacing.
High-pressure torsion will improve the chemical and mechanical integrity of interfaces between lamellae.
Intense post-solidification deformation processing can refine the grain structure of a high-entropy alloy.
HPT-induced grain refinement will increase tensile strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Refined lamellar spacing and stronger interfaces will produce a more uniform load distribution.
Improved interfacial cohesion and reduced lamellar spacing will reduce local stress concentrations.
Reduced stress concentrations will delay microcrack initiation and thereby improve tensile ductility.
HPT-processed samples will have higher room-temperature tensile strength than conventionally processed samples.
HPT-processed samples will have greater room-temperature elongation at fracture than conventionally processed samples.
Conventionally processed coarse lamellar colonies exhibit early microcrack initiation leading to brittle failure.
The intervention requires uniform lamellar refinement without excessive processing defects.
Formation of detrimental secondary phases can prevent the proposed strength–ductility improvement.
The magnitude of the response will depend on HPT pressure and number of revolutions.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements will depend on alloy composition.
